tour.title: Project Overview: Settings and Routing
tour.description: Start with settings.py, which registers the bounded-context apps and middleware, and urls.py, which routes requests to the tracking view. These are the entry points that show how the DDD-structured cargo tracker is assembled into a Django project.

tour.title: Ubiquitous Language: The Glossary
tour.description: The handling GLOSSARY defines the shared vocabulary of the domain. Reading it before the code makes the names used in later steps (handling events, cargo, voyage) easier to follow.

tour.title: Cargo Aggregate and Value Objects
tour.description: The Cargo aggregate root combines a tracking id, route specification, itinerary and delivery. Building on the glossary, these value objects hold the business rules independent of Django.

tour.title: Supporting Contexts: Handling, Voyage, Location
tour.description: Handling events and history, voyages with schedules and carrier movements, and UN/LOCODE locations are separate bounded contexts. Each defines its own domain objects and repository ports that the cargo context relies on.

tour.title: Persistence with the Django ORM
tour.description: ORM models and repository implementations adapt the domain ports to the database, keeping the domain free of framework code. Migrations create the underlying tables.

tour.title: Application Service and Composition Root
tour.description: The tracking application service looks up a cargo and its handling history, and the composition root wires the Django repositories into it. This is where domain and infrastructure meet.

tour.title: The Tracking Interface
tour.description: The tracking view handles the form, calls the application service and renders results using presentation helpers for status text, ETA, next activity and history.

tour.title: Templates and the Map Frame
tour.description: Django templates use a base layout with htmx for the tracking page and result partial, while the map frame embeds a Leaflet map fed by coordinates and an adapter.

tour.title: Sample Data and Entry Points
tour.description: The seed_sample_data command loads sample cargos, events and voyages through the Django repositories, and the WSGI/ASGI modules expose the app to servers.
